keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the principle (memory consolidation turns fragile new memories into stable, long-lasting ones) and the conclusion (sleep is not the opposite of studying but the final step of learning). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why do many teenagers feel wide awake at midnight but exhausted in the morning?
qs.qko: 왜 많은 십 대가 자정에는 말똥말똥한데 아침에는 몹시 피곤할까요?
opts: Their body clocks naturally shift later during adolescence
They drink too much water before bed
Their hippocampus stops working at night
evs: Their body clocks naturally shift later during adolescence, so many feel wide awake at midnight but exhausted at seven in the morning.
However, sleep is not a magic shortcut.
In addition, timing matters, since sleeping soon after learning tends to help more than sleeping much later.
Later, during REM sleep, when most vivid dreams happen, the brain seems to connect new information with what it already knows.
why: 본문에 사춘기에는 몸속 시계가 자연스럽게 뒤로 밀려서, 자정에는 말똥말똥하고 아침 일곱 시에는 몹시 피곤하다고 나와요.
The text says their body clocks naturally shift later during adolescence, so many feel awake at midnight but exhausted at seven in the morning.

qs.q: In the text, what does "sleep is not a magic shortcut" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «sleep is not a magic shortcut» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Sleep strengthens what you really studied, but it cannot replace studying
Sleep makes you smarter even if you never study
Short naps are better than a long night of sleep
evs: It strengthens memories that were formed through real effort, but it cannot create knowledge that was never studied.
As a result, people often solve problems more easily after a good night's sleep.
Many students believe that sleep is wasted time, but scientists now see it as an active part of learning.
Therefore, the smartest study plan includes both focused review and enough sleep.
why: 바로 다음 문장에서 잠은 실제로 노력해서 만든 기억을 강하게 할 뿐, 공부한 적 없는 지식을 만들어 낼 수는 없다고 해요. 그래서 잠은 공부를 건너뛰게 해 주는 마법의 지름길이 아니에요.
Sleep strengthens memories formed through real effort, but it cannot create knowledge that was never studied. It is not a shortcut around studying.

qs.q: Why do people often solve problems more easily after a good night's sleep?
qs.qko: 푹 자고 나면 왜 문제를 더 쉽게 푸는 경우가 많을까요?
opts: During REM sleep, the brain connects new information with what it already knows
The brain switches off completely, so it gets a full rest
People dream about the answers in their textbooks
evs: Later, during REM sleep, when most vivid dreams happen, the brain seems to connect new information with what it already knows.
As a result, people often solve problems more easily after a good night's sleep.
A small part of the brain called the hippocampus stores new experiences for a short time.
Health experts generally recommend about eight to ten hours of sleep a night for teenagers, yet many get far less.
why: 렘수면 동안 뇌는 새 정보를 이미 알고 있는 것과 연결하고, 그 결과 푹 자고 나면 문제를 더 쉽게 푼다고 해요. 두 문장을 이어 봐야 해요.
During REM sleep, the brain seems to connect new information with what it already knows. As a result, people often solve problems more easily.
